name: Atayal
catalog_quote: Stress in all Atayal dialects in this study is always word-final, and is not discussed separately for each dialect. It is realized as a pitch drop, and stressed syllables also have a higher intensity. Penultimate syllables tend to have a rising pitch in anticipation of the final pitch drop. I believe it is this rising pitch in penultimate syllables that led some linguists to occasionally hear pen…

audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim at Goderich 2020 pp.31-32 (PDF 51-52) in the held file, with two further held confirmations (p.41, p.113). Deciding source: a 2020 phonology dissertation on seven dialects from the author's own fieldwork — the most recent and broadest phonological description of Atayal; it explicitly addresses and explains away the penultimate-stress reports (Li 1981:239, C. Chen 2011:32). Independent sources opened today agree on word-final stress: Lambert 1999 (acoustically verified for Mabalay C'uli', ROA-342 p.17 and appendix), H.-S. Lin 2015 pp.76/93 for Wulai/Mrqwang Squliq ('generally falls on the last syllable'), and StressTyp2's Egerod 1966 coding; H. Huang 2018 (abstract seen) builds Squliq on an iambic right-edge foot. The one dissent is a held source, Rau 1992 p.26 (Wulai Squliq: penult or final by root, penult-stressed roots re-analysed as long

sources.quote: p.76 (Squliq of Wulai and Mrqwang): 'Stress generally falls on the last syllable of a word. Squliq Atayal has two important phonological features. First, there is a rule of vowel reduction that changes all pre-penultimate vowels to ə (Egerod 1965, 1980; Li 1980, 1981; H. Huang 2006b; Rau 1992).' p.93: 'Since stress in Squliq Atayal generally falls on the last syllable, the foot that stands at the right edge of the word should constitute the main stress foot'.
sources.locator: p.76 (PDF p.102) §2.1 Squliq Atayal phonology; p.93 (PDF p.119)

sources.citation: Lambert, Wendy Mae. 1999. Epenthesis, metathesis, and vowel-glide alternation: prosodic reflexes in Mabalay Atayal. MA thesis, National Tsing Hua University. Rutgers Optimality Archive ROA-342 (227 pp).
sources.quote: p.17: 'In Mabalay, stress falls on the final syllable of the word. This has been verified in an acoustic analysis ... In this respect, Mabalay differs from the Wulai dialect, where stress is on the penultimate syllable when the penultimate vowel is long (approximately 80% of the data); otherwise, stress is on the ultimate syllable, (Rau, 1992). The Taoyuan dialect also has long vowels, but they do not affect stress (Li, 1980).' ... 'The pronominal enclitics are generally not stressed ... They are not part of the prosodic word'. sources.quote: Instrumental duration study of word-final long vs short high vowels (5 speakers, carrier sentence); finds the final length contrast eroding. Says nothing about stress position beyond p.12 'it is reported that stress and intonation affect the duration, but it is still not clear to the author how'.
